Reff is the LHS output. The four quantities described as program-setting inputs (R0, q, d, a) are the natural sampling axes and get ranges; the remaining eight free symbols are fixed physical/program constants. Parameter values chosen in sensible epidemiological magnitudes (recovery rate gamma=0.2/day ~ 5-day infectious period; kappa,beta,phi ~ 0.5; eta=0.1; alpha=0.3/day; rho, sigma at mid-range of the suggested bounds). check_substitution at a central point gives finite real Reff=1.80. excitation_check confirms the full signal at 60*sigma and the newly added residual-amplification factor at 8.19*sigma, both well above the 5*sigma threshold.

scenario_text: Contact tracing and isolation remove detected infectious individuals from circulation at a rate depending on surveillance intensity. Analysts measure the instantaneous net reproduction number as a function of baseline transmissibility, isolation efficiency, and detection delay. This is evaluated as an algebraic control outcome across sampled program settings. Underlying contact structure and recovery rate are fixed background conditions.
